from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Prerequisite: The Antipodal Mapping", [
            "Consider a sphere, the surface S².",
            "Points x and -x are antipodal.",
            "They sit exactly opposite each other."
        ])
        
        # Assets
        sphere = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg", fill_opacity=0.3, color=WHITE)
        label_s2 = Text("S²", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        
        # Group sphere and label
        sphere_group = VGroup(sphere, label_s2)
        self.place_in_area(sphere_group, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Repositioning based on feedback (overriding place_in_area positions for individual control if needed)
        sphere.move_to(self.grid['D4']).scale(0.6)
        label_s2.move_to(self.grid['B4']).scale(0.7)
        
        x = Dot(color="#FF0000")
        x.move_to(sphere.get_center() + 0.8 * RIGHT)
        minus_x = Dot(color="#0000FF")
        minus_x.move_to(sphere.get_center() + 0.8 * LEFT)
        line = DashedLine(x.get_center(), minus_x.get_center(), color=YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(sphere), Write(label_s2))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(x), FadeIn(minus_x))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.play(Flash(x), Flash(minus_x))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#0000FF")
        
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Stolen Necklace Problem", [
            "Thieves must divide a beaded necklace.",
            "Each needs half of every bead type.",
            "This is the discrete necklace problem."
        ])
        
        # Assets
        beads_asset = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/beads.svg")

        self.place_at_grid(beads_asset, 'B3', scale_factor=0.6)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        thief_a = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=GREEN).set_opacity(0.2)
        thief_b = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=ORANGE).set_opacity(0.2)
        thief_boxes = VGroup(thief_a, thief_b).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.0)
        
        divider_lines = VGroup(Line(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color=WHITE), Line(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color=WHITE))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "We map discrete cuts to a sphere.",
            "Fair division becomes a zero-sum function.",
            "Borsuk-Ulam guarantees an exact fair solution."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mathematical Bridge", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        necklace = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/necklace.svg", color=YELLOW)
        sphere = Circle(radius=1.2, color=BLUE)
        point = Dot(color=RED)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # We map discrete cuts to a sphere.
        self.place_in_area(necklace, "B4", "B6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(necklace))
        self.wait(1)
        
        necklace_loop = Arc(radius=0.6, start_angle=0, angle=2*PI, color=YELLOW)
        self.play(Transform(necklace, necklace_loop))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Fair division becomes a zero-sum function.
        self.place_in_area(sphere, "D4", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(sphere))
        
        self.place_at_grid(point, "C3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(point))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Borsuk-Ulam guarantees an exact fair solution.
        # Reuse necklace asset as reference
        ref_necklace = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/necklace.svg", color=GREEN).scale(0.3)
        ref_necklace.move_to(self.grid["C3"])
        self.play(FadeIn(ref_necklace))
        
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(self.grid["D5"]))
        self.play(point.animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(2)

        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Application", [

            "Fair division is mathematically guaranteed.",

        # Elements
        pile_a = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.15, color=RED, fill_opacity=1) for _ in range(5)],

                         *[Circle(radius=0.15, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=1) for _ in range(5)]).arrange_in_grid(2, 5, buff=0.1)
        piles = VGroup(pile_a, pile_b).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)

        # SVG Assets
        people = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/people.svg", color=WHITE)
        scissors = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/scissors.svg", color=WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_in_area(piles, 'B2', 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(piles))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.place_at_grid(scissors, 'D3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(people, 'D5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(scissors), FadeIn(people))
        self.play(Flash(scissors))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(TEAL))
        fair_text = Text("Fair division is mathematically guaranteed", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(fair_text, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)

outline.topic: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem and the Stolen Necklace Problem
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in mathematics or computer science

sections.title: Intuitive Prerequisite: The Antipodal Mapping
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a sphere (S²) and the idea of 'antipodal points'—two points exactly opposite each other. Visualize this as North and South poles, or any two points x and -x.
sections.example: An animation showing a globe where if you touch a point in Tokyo, the corresponding antipodal point is in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean.

sections.title: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem
sections.content: State the core theorem: Any continuous function from an n-sphere to n-dimensional Euclidean space must map at least one pair of antipodal points to the same value. Use a 'Temperature/Pressure' analogy.
sections.example: Visualizing a map of the Earth: At any given time, there must be at least two antipodal points on the surface with the exact same temperature and air pressure.

sections.title: Transition: The Necklace Problem
sections.content: Define the 'Stolen Necklace' problem: Two thieves steal a necklace with k types of beads. How can they cut the necklace to divide the beads fairly (each getting exactly half of each type)? Introduce the concept of a 'discrete' problem mapped to a 'continuous' sphere.
sections.example: A colorful necklace with 10 red beads and 10 blue beads. The goal is to cut the string into segments so that both thieves end up with 5 red and 5 blue beads.

sections.title: The Mathematical Bridge
sections.content: Explain how the discrete necklace arrangement is embedded into a continuous space. By modeling the possible cuts as points on a sphere, the fair distribution becomes a 'zero-sum' function that satisfies the Borsuk-Ulam condition.
sections.example: Animation showing the necklace being stretched into a line, then wrapped around a sphere where the 'cuts' are coordinates on the sphere's surface.

sections.title: Conclusion and Application
sections.content: Summarize how a deep topological result provides a concrete algorithmic solution for resource sharing. Emphasize that fair division is mathematically guaranteed by the curvature of space.
sections.example: A final visual of two characters, Alice and Bob, perfectly splitting a 'necklace' of resources using a pair of scissors, representing the Borsuk-Ulam solution.
